messages:
maya: Quick thought — proposal to add an explicit residency header so we can serve local-active for privacy-sensitive tenants while keeping active/active control plane. Idea: X-Redwood-Residency: eu_only|global and X-Redwood-Consent-Stamp: <sha>. That lets edge proxies prefer local caches and model variants. How do folks feel about failover safety and runbook complexity?

arun: I like the intent but worried about split-brain. If two regions accept writes we need a deterministic reconciliation plan. The header helps routing but doesn't solve write finality.

sofie: For PII-tagged tenants we could do local synchronous commit + async replication to other regions via an escrow queue. On failover we quarantine non-ack'd escrow items until operator verifies jurisdictional constraints. ops-bot: created ticket R-4523 for escrow-runbook. :white_check_mark: 

ben: Can we use a lease-based gating mechanism? Tenant gets a short region-lease (ttl=30s) held by the primary region. Other regions only accept writes if they can verify lease expiry or receive an explicit takeover token. That reduces conflicting writes without full global locking.

maya: Sketch of header + lease flow: 
```
Client -> Edge (adds X-Redwood-Residency: eu_only)
Edge -> Local proxy checks residency cache (fast)
if (lease.exists(tenant) && lease.owner == local_region) { serve locally }
else if (local_model_variant.available) { serve locally with quantized variant + mark replicate_async }
else { forward to global primary with X-Redwood-Residency-Fallback: remote }
```
We'd also return X-Redwood-Consent-Stamp so client can cache that for short TTL.

laura: Telemetry notes: we should emit metrics sample: resident.local_hit, resident.remote_fallback, resident.takeover_attempts, escrow.queue_depth. Also log consent-stamp with sample of tenant ID (hashed) to meet audit.

arun: Rollout plan: canary on 5% of EU tenants, monitor divergence rate (conflicting-writes/sec), tail latency, and escrow backlog. If divergence > threshold -> automatic rollback.

sofie: Operator runbook (short):
- Step 1: check lease status `rwctl leases show tenant:<id>`
- Step 2: prewarm local model variant: `curl -X POST https://ops.prewarm/models/prewarm -d '{"model":"gptq-local","tenant":"<id>"}'`
- Step 3: drain incoming remote-forwarding: set router flag `set-route <tenant> freeze-remote-forward true`
- Step 4: inspect escrow queue: `escrowctl peek tenant:<id>` and reconcile.

ben: A couple of concerns: quantized local variants may change output distribution -> need eval gating and rollback hooks. Also cost: prewarming per-tenant could be expensive unless we use a warm-cache heuristic.

maya: Agreed — include a model-variant compatibility score in Optimize. Keep default fallback to remote primary for high-risk tenants, and local-only for tenants that opt-in with legal approval.

laura: For auditing, capture consent-stamp and lease events in the audit log stream (immutable). Add a retention flag for compliance customers.

arun: How about takeover safety? If local region loses network and another region attempts takeover, require a three-way handshake: takeover-request -> origin-region-heartbeat-check -> takeover-commit. If heartbeat unresponsive for > lease-ttl*2 then allow commit. That reduces split-brain.

sofie: +1 to handshake. Also add operator-confirmed emergency takeover mode (manual) with forced quarantine of escrowed writes.

maya: Action items I can pick up: 1) RFC doc with header spec + sample proxies, 2) small prototype in edge-proxy that honors X-Redwood-Residency and returns consent-stamp, 3) metrics dashboard for divergence and escrow. Will open RFC PR.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staged rollout created: chart/residency-fallback v0.1 -> canary 5% (ops ticket R-4523).

ben: :thumbsup: keep the eval guard rails tight.

laura: I'll add the audit retention checkbox to enterprise onboarding docs.

maya: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC link once PR is up.
